messages:
anna: Heads up 1: we have a converted hire (Sofia M) who was employed via GlobalHire from 2025-02-10 to 2025-05-31 and moved to Redwood payroll on 2025-06-01. GlobalHire withheld employee 401(k) deferrals and forwarded their employer match for FebMay. Sofia is asking whether those dollars can be moved into our Fidelity account and whether the FebMay period can count toward Redwood service for 401(k) eligibility and vesting.

sofia: Hi team 1: I can provide paystubs and the GlobalHire contribution export. Curious about any impact to my 2025 elective deferral limit and catch-up contributions (I turned 50 in March).

benefits-team: Short answer: incoming rollovers of employee deferrals are typically possible (trustee-to-trustee). Employer match/backdating and service credit depend on plan docs and vendor discretion. We'll need the contribution ledger and plan doc to start.

finance-payroll: Operational note: if we accept a retro employer contribution, payroll must record it in the correct tax year and box codes. Vendors sometimes limit backdated employer contributions to a window (e.g., 90 days). If outside that, we can still accept rollover of employee funds but not a retro match.

anna: Okay. What exactly should Sofia request from GlobalHire to avoid rounds of follow-ups?

benefits-team: Ask GlobalHire for: 1) contribution ledger CSV with columns: pay date, pay period end, employee pretax, employee Roth, employer match (amount & formula), and date funds remitted to plan; 2) plan document & summary plan description; 3) any participant statement showing vested %; 4) confirmation whether contributions were remitted to a named TPA/provider (include contact info).

sofia: Sending that now. Quick follow-up: the GlobalHire export shows $9,800 in employee deferrals YTD. Does that mean I only have $3,200 of deferral room left for 2025 (given the $13,000 limit for under-50 in my example)? Also, does rolling those funds into Fidelity double-count them?

benefits-team: The amounts withheld by GlobalHire that were salary deferrals count toward your 2025 elective deferral limit. A rollover of those deferrals into Fidelity does NOT create additional deferral counts; it just moves existing dollars. Catch-up rules: since you turned 50 in March, you're eligible for catch-up contributions for 2025, assuming plan allows catch-up. We'll reconcile exact numbers once we have the ledger.

finance-payroll: If you already hit $9,800 via GlobalHire, you have remaining elective deferral room up to the statutory limit for 2025. We'll coordinate with you to prevent double-withholding. If needed, we can set up a year-to-date deferral reconciliation after rollover.

globalhire-bot: Automated message: Contribution package uploaded for Sofia M (file: GH_SofiaM_2025_FEB_MAY.csv). Plan: GlobalHire Flex 401k. Plan admin contact: planadmin@globalhire.com.

anna: Great 1: benefits, can you open the transfer case with Fidelity and ask: (a) whether the provided ledger suffices for a trustee-to-trustee rollover, (b) whether vendor will accept backdated employer match and credit service for vesting, and (c) any vendor cutoff dates we should know?

benefits-team: On it. Expect vendor reply in ~7 business days. If Fidelity declines backdating, we'll discuss options: 1) accept employee rollover only, 2) consider discretionary company contribution (requires approvals), or 3) document denial and proceed prospectively.

sofia: Thanks everyone 1: I'll upload signed authorization and confirm my SSN last 4 for the request. Appreciate the help. :pray:

anna: Thanks @sofia. I'll track this for open enrollment readiness.
